answer: The 17th century BCE is when Diversity in Pottery Form collapses while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneously.

payload.hypothesis: The 17th century BCE is when Diversity in Pottery Form collapses while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneously.
payload.workflow: Used the 37 raw 100-yr bin values from time_series_data.csv (PotteryForm and PotteryDecoration columns, one point every 100 years from CE -4100 to -500). Computed first-differences (diff) on the 100-yr grid for both series, then flagged bins where Form collapses (ΔForm < -0.5) AND Decoration increases (ΔDeco > +0.5). Exactly one bin qualified: CE -1700, where ΔForm = -1.87 (0.74 → -1.13, the largest negative Form delta in the series) and ΔDeco = +1.45 (-0.48 → 0.97). An adjacent-bin (±100 yr) robustness check found no other qualifying bin in the window, confirming the event is isolated. CE -1700 = 1700 BCE, which maps to the 17th century BCE. (Note: signals are Z-standardised, so 'collapse'/'increase' are relative to the long-run mean, not absolute counts.) capital.csv cross-check: BCE 1700 row (ZKeform -1.13, Zkeverz 0.97) mirrors the same time_series point.
